{
  "screen_decision": "exclude",
  "screen_rationale": "The study exclusively uses in vitro methods (human-induced pluripotent stem cells, microphysiological systems, MEA) to assess drug effects. It does not involve whole, live non-human animals as the index test. Therefore, it does not meet the inclusion criteria for a systematic review of animal model concordance.",
  "arm": "disease-biology",
  "arm_evidence": "The study investigates the effects of vanoxerine on human cardiac excitation-contraction coupling parameters and predicts proarrhythmic potential using in vitro models.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "cardiovascular"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "The study focuses on cardiotoxicity, specifically vanoxerine-induced proarrhythmic potential and its effects on cardiac electrophysiology and contractility.",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "The study utilizes two distinct in vitro models: a complex cardiac microphysiological system (MPS) and a human-induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocyte (hiPSC-CM) multielectrode array (MEA) CiPA model.",
  "species": [
    "not-species-specific"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The study exclusively uses human-induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) and does not involve any non-human animal species.",
  "endpoint_class": "secondary-biomarker",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The study measures parameters such as action potential duration, calcium transient duration, and field potential duration, which are biomarkers of cardiac function and potential toxicity."
}
